title: Vault daemon-churn: decide on global basic-memory ensure_frontmatter_on_sync=false (operator-owned — affects all 24 bm projects)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the perpetual vault git-churn + a latent corruption risk. basic-memory's daemon has ensure_frontmatter_on_sync=true (~/.basic-memory/config.json, GLOBAL to all 24 projects), so on every sync it re-serializes vault/**/*.md frontmatter: adds 'permalink: a-plus-maxing/<path>' (206/539 files lack it), folds long titles, strips trailing newlines — and DESTRUCTIVELY mangles {placeholder}/flow-collection/inline-comment YAML on template files (e.g. _template.md: 'name: {x}' -> 'name:\n  x: null'). Never committed (the stash-and-discard pattern protected against it), so no data lost, but it's the churn source + a corruption risk if ever committed.

COMPLETE FIX (operator's call — global, affects 23 other bm projects): set ensure_frontmatter_on_sync=false in ~/.basic-memory/config.json (a .bak exists), restart the bm daemon, then 'git restore vault/' in a-plus-maxing -> permanently clean tree. Effect elsewhere: daemon stops auto-injecting permalink-frontmatter into hand-authored files on sync; write_note-created notes are unaffected (frontmatter added at write time); indexing/search/link-resolution still work (title/path fallback). Trivially reversible. No per-project scope exists (one global config + one shared memory.db).

INTERIM (in place now): the don't-commit-vault-daemon-churn discipline + the cross-worktree model are documented in CLAUDE.md (Conventions). Optional hardening: quote template {placeholders} so the daemon's re-serialization is idempotent even if churn is committed.

title: Cap DNA-export decompression size in dna.land (review SEC-205-01)
description: PR #205 /review-pr security finding SEC-205-01 (conf 90, impact 3). dna.land copies a zip member / reads a .txt UNBOUNDED: a 204KB zip → a 209MB landed file (1027x amplification); a 150MB single-line .txt → 477MB RSS. A hostile/malformed 'export' fills local disk or OOMs the process instead of being rejected — the module docstring claims fail-loud on a wrong file, but an oversized file is silently accepted. REALISM LOW: operator-owns-the-file (self-DoS), local-only, no egress. This is DEFENSIVE PROGRAMMING → needs operator sign-off per the no-unmotivated-defense rule (motivation: hostile/malformed export → local DoS). FIX (if approved): stream the zip-member copy with a running byte counter, raise ValueError past a generous ceiling (~100-200MB; real 23andMe ~15-25MB), delete the partial on raise; same size check on the .txt path via source.stat().st_size. Deferred from PR #205 — operator decision required.
notes: S85 wave-A security review (MED-2): the uncapped zip-member decompression now ALSO exists in scripts/ingest/adapters/healthkit.py:124-125 (Apple Health export.xml extraction, mirroring dna.land) — executed: a 510KiB zip extracted a 500MiB member (1029x), and dna.land 514x. Disk exhaustion (memory bounded: copyfileobj streams to disk, iterparse clears). DEFERRED per operator (07f6 still open, revisit later). When addressed, cap BOTH dna.py:96-97 and healthkit.py:124-125 with a running byte-counter + unlink-partial-on-over (the multipart _stage_file pattern). Note: the multipart UPLOAD ceiling (512MiB compressed) does NOT bound the decompressed member.

title: extract_chunked.extract_all silently drops non-conformant readings at the swappable client seam

title: ingest: re-ingest cannot correct a stored reading's value (dedupe excludes value, first-write-wins)
description: PR #47 review TEST-006/BUG-004: the dedupe key is (item,timepoint,source) per ADR-0002; value is excluded. So a corrected value re-entered via import_csv or manual_entry for an already-stored (item,timepoint,source) silently dedupes away — the operator's correction is dropped with no warning. Pinned as first-write-wins by a committed test in PR #47. Real product gap for a health tracker (mis-entered values can't be fixed by re-ingest). notes:
S51 adjudication (2026-06-12, Walter adopted the recommendation): SUPERSEDING-APPEND with latest-wins read semantics — ADR-0002 append-only Y-statement PRESERVED, audit trail kept; a correction appends a new line and readers resolve most-recent-wins. Surface choice: store-level primitive first (explicit correct/overwrite entry point at the CLI/ingest layer); any future edit-layer bottoms out in it (ADR-0004 zero-script artifacts cannot host editing). BUILD next session: read-semantics change touches ALL consumers (loop_schema, dashboard data layer, render_views) — needs the Factory-to-Component wiring sweep + an ADR-0002 amendment under change-control.

title: [PR#44/BUG-06] store.append dedupe is a non-atomic check-then-act (concurrent-append race)
description: scripts/store/store.py append reads the dedupe set, tests membership, then writes with no lock; two concurrent appends of the same reading both pass the check and write a duplicate, violating the idempotency contract. Low likelihood in V1 single-operator local use; fix when concurrent ingestion is added (fcntl.flock on the item file, or atomic dedupe-aware write). Deferred from PR #44 review (out of V1 threat model).
notes:
S51 adjudication (2026-06-12, Walter adopted the recommendation): KEEP DEFERRED — no concurrent writer exists on main, so the bead's own trigger condition has not fired; adding flock ahead of need is speculative under the no-defensive-programming rule. ACCURATE SYMPTOM (post-PR#46 atomic rewrite): the risk class is LOST UPDATES under concurrent append (read-modify-write race across _read_lines -> os.replace), NOT the stale duplicate-line symptom the description names. If/when a concurrent ingestion path is added, build then: sibling-lockfile flock was briefed as the lighter option vs an atomic dedupe-aware write redesign — sequenced after any further store-surface work.

S52 (2026-06-12, PR #105 review): the unlocked read-modify-write now has a SECOND writer (store.correct) and a new lost-update shape — a concurrent append that snapshots before a correction's os.replace lands rewrites the file WITHOUT the superseding line (the correction silently reverts). Adjudication unchanged (KEEP DEFERRED — no concurrent writer installed; flock ahead of need is speculative); this note records the new shape so the bead's build brief covers both writers when its trigger fires.

S53 (#108 review F-I): the S51 adjudication text above was destroyed by the S52 notes update (bd update --notes REPLACES; authored as an append) and restored from git history at the #108 review. bd notes updates are read-modify-write.

title: [PR#69/BUG-3] scheduler adapter import has no error isolation — one bad module aborts the unattended run
description: S40 Tier-3 Bug Hunter BUG-3 (conf 80). _wired_adapters() calls importlib.import_module on every adapters/*.py with no try/except; a single module that raises at import (bad transitive import, missing optional dep, top-level error) propagates out and kills scheduler.run() for ALL healthy wired adapters in an unattended, no-operator run — contradicting the 'completes unattended, exit 0 over the wired set' contract. The non-defensive part (instantiating non-conformant classes) is fixed in the Tier-3 round via issubclass(obj, Adapter)-before-instantiate (BUG-1/SEC-2). BUG-3's fix is a try/except around per-module import+construction (skip+surface the failing module) — that is DEFENSIVE programming, which per project policy needs explicit motivation + user approval before adding. Motivation: unattended-run availability (one bad adapter shouldn't take down ingestion). Decide fail-fast-and-document vs skip-and-surface with Walter before implementing.

title: Metered loop_dispatch needs a judge/lens surface (specialist-only breaks the gated loop)
description: BLOCKING precondition for arming the live metered /plan-loop (ADR-0049 D1). Tier-3 (Bug-Hunter F1 + Contracts REJECT, S141, EXECUTED): the loop_dispatch(name,prompt,context) seam is a 3-name-space aggregate (specialist / quality-judge / safety-lens; plan_loop.dispatch_route_collisions + the module-level assert at plan_loop.py:109 enforce disjointness). metered_dispatch.build_dispatch routes EVERY name through client.author(name,context), and ModelClient.author ALWAYS returns a plan-author envelope {specialist,recommendations} — never a judge {dimension:score} map or a lens findings-list. EXECUTED: judge -> REVISE-always; lens -> AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'get' -> caught -> SAFETY_BLOCKED. A live /plan-loop deterministically produces 0 plans after burning metered spend on 6 author calls. FIX: the metered client needs a .judge(payload)->{dimension:score} + a lens ->[findings] path (or the dispatch must branch on name into distinct metered model calls with distinct output schemas), so the metered lane serves all 3 name-spaces like the subscription session does. Until this lands, main() must NOT arm the metered loop_dispatch (reverted in the ADR-0049-T1 remediation, S141 — the metered SPECIALIST dispatch + D2 egress scan DID land + are mock-proven). This is the unscheduled build-plan gap: ADR-0049-T1 builds the specialist dispatch, T2 reuses the same loop_dispatch — neither builds the judge/lens surface.
notes: ADDED (ADR-0049-T2 doc-gate Arch-F5, S144): when this bead arms the metered loop_dispatch, it MUST ALSO wire a consumer for the ADR-0049-T2 'plan-update-cadence' store intent — the schedule setting records the operator's Off/Weekly/Daily cadence as an append-only store reading (source:settings, last-by-timepoint = current), read back by the Profile UI but consumed by NO scheduler today. When the daily/auto-run enable path lands (glzi), it reads this intent stream; until then a 'weekly' intent sits unread while the operator may believe it took effect. Also: arming loop_dispatch makes the ADR-0049-T2 'Update my plan now' trigger a LIVE forced-spend surface (today it hits the honest-degraded {reason:loop-dispatch-unavailable} at 0 spend) — the trigger inherits the arming.

title: Worktree-blind PreToolUse git hooks: block-commit-main false-positives + block-pii-commit vacuous pass for worktree commits
description: Surfaced S51 (2026-06-11) by the parallel worktree build fan-out. VERIFIED FIRSTHAND: block-commit-main.sh denied a commit in worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-* on branch fix/scheduler-typed-unwired-marker while the MAIN checkout sat on main; after moving the main checkout to fix/s51-close the identical commit passed. The hook resolves PROJECT_ROOT/HEAD from its own script path (the main checkout), not the repo receiving the commit. Consequence A: false-positive INV-BRANCH-NOT-MAIN denials for every worktree agent whenever the checkout is on main (drove one build agent to an sh -c bypass — disclosed in its report; bypass also skipped block-pii-commit + block-ungated-vault-write for those commits; content verified clean + git-native pre-push scan ran at push). Consequence B (the real hole): block-pii-commit's staged-set content scan inspects the MAIN checkout's staged set for worktree commits — vacuous pass — so worktree commits are PII-unscanned at the commit layer; the git-native pre-push-pii-scan.sh is the only content backstop (worktrees share .git so it does run at push). Same PROJECT_ROOT pattern in block-ungated-vault-write.sh. Fix direction: resolve the target repo from the PreToolUse hook input's cwd (the tool call's working directory) instead of SCRIPT_DIR/../..; add worktree fixtures to the hook smoke suites (a worktree commit on a fix branch must PASS block-commit-main; a worktree commit staging PII content must FAIL block-pii-commit). Hook edits need per-session authorization — schedule as its own authorized unit.
close_reason: Closed by PR #107 (main e8b0dd8): the three settings.json hooks resolve their target repo worktree-aware via .claude/hooks/lib/resolve-target-repo.sh (cwd > env > script-path; target_is_this_repo scopes gates to this trunk — foreign repos pass clean), scanner pinned to the shipping checkout, lib-load failure denies in the PII hook. New 12-case lib suite + scope fixtures in all three hook suites (34/67/17). Reviewed 6-agent full methodology, blind-verified 8/8.

title: DECISION: third-party PHI (provider/MRN) in health-substance free-text reaches the planner — un-park de-id for it, or accept per 'all health substance flows'?
notes: PR#330 Tier-3 review, F1 third-party-ID part (blind-triage verdict: DECISION, not auto-fixable). context_assembler.assemble_context carries allowlisted health-substance FREE-TEXT (medication-list, raw-lab-values, clinical-notes, raw-symptom-free-text) RAW to the no-train model (generate_plan.py:356→client.author, NO downstream backstop). pii_scan.scan_operator_value catches ONLY the OPERATOR's own identity/contact + structural email/phone/postal/DOB/>=9-digit — NOT third-party names (prescriber/provider/facility) or short/grouped MRN/insurance-id. So a clinical note / med list / lab report free-text carrying 'Dr. Jane Smith, CVS #1234 (MRN 55019)' reaches the model. ADR-0042 §2 PARKED de-id ('all health substance flows; do not widen a de-id scheme'), and the import-time partition assertion classes these as health-substance-not-identity — so this is a CONSEQUENCE of the parked-de-id decision, not a defect. The GENOTYPE sub-case (a raw rsID+allele in that free-text) IS fixed in PR#330 (it breaches the explicit 'raw genotypes never cross' crown-jewel exception). OPTIONS for the operator: (a) accept (all health substance flows, single-operator local no-train lane, low reachability) + document the residual; (b) un-park de-id for third-party identifiers — add a structural provider/MRN scrub to the carried free-text (reuse pii_scan structural classes); (c) drop clinical-notes/medication-list/raw-lab-values from the allowlist (the curated rx-interaction-classes/active-issue-class coarse tokens already flow — but loses the rich free-text the re-architecture wanted). Must land before the operator-present LIVE run + before any structured ingestion adapter writes these fields at volume.

title: Harden pdf_extract subprocess: abspath/-- + timeout (ADR-0031 W1 Security LOW)
description: Wave-1 Tier-2 Security review (PASS) flagged 2 LOW defense-in-depth items on scripts/ingest/pdf_extract.py, both UNREACHABLE in the integrated T4 path under the single-operator threat model + defensive (need operator sign-off per the no-unapproved-defensive-programming rule): LOW-1 — the staged PDF path is passed as a positional subprocess argv token with no '--' option-terminator and not resolved absolute, so a path whose basename is exactly a poppler/marker option could be parsed as a flag (argument injection). Remediation: bounded timeout= + let TimeoutExpired fail loud through PdfExtractError (constant message, no path interpolation). Fold into the T4 wiring or a follow-up. The RISKY-1 contract fix (wrap OSError->PdfExtractError) landed in W1; if the timeout is added, also wrap TimeoutExpired.

title: OQ-5 wiring: bound the held-lock converse under confirm_plan_change with a per-request timeout

title: Google authorize leg omits access_type=offline -> no refresh_token at LIVE

DISTINCT from the beaded PKCE-vs-confidential Google conflict (trfs — that's which client model; this is the authorize-param precondition). FIX: add a per-vendor _build_authorize_url extra_params seam (Google: access_type=offline, prompt=consent) + an authorize-URL assertion. title: secret_store fallback-tier concurrent set_secret is last-writer-wins (lost update)
description: Phase-4 Security review of the ADR-0048-T3 recipe (sec-r48 LOW-4, CONTRACT-ESCALATION): secret_store._fallback_write (~__init__.py:191-194) is read-whole-dict -> set one key -> os.replace whole file. os.replace prevents a TORN file but NOT a lost update: two concurrent set_secret calls last-writer-wins on the whole map, so a concurrently-written SIBLING source's token silently reverts to absent ('disconnected'; re-save fixes). PRE-EXISTING T1 property — but ADR-0048-T3 newly exposes a browser-driven concurrent write surface (ThreadingHTTPServer = thread per request; multiple tabs / rapid connect-all POST /settings/tracker), where before all set_secret writes came from the sequential unattended oauth_pull tick. FALLBACK TIER ONLY (keyring primary writes each service independently, no shared-dict race). No leak, no cross-source value corruption — data-integrity/availability only. FIX in secret_store (T1 owner): serialize the fallback read-modify-write under a lock, or per-service files. NOT a defensive patch in the server handler.

title: 0045-T3 LOW-1: move daily _read_standing inside cadence_lock (Tier-4 TOCTOU)
description: Security Tier-2 LOW-1 (Wave-6/ADR-0045-T3, commit 0fdafb3b). daily_monitor.run reads _read_standing + the version_date snapshot OUTSIDE cadence_lock (daily_monitor.py:194), before the acquire (:208); the stale snapshot then drives the in-lock Tier-4 mark_pending(domain, version_date, root) safety hold. UNREACHABLE in the shipped artifact (both cadences disabled-by-default; the daily-interval enable that co-arms them is deferred to glzi). THREAT once co-armed: a concurrent weekly tick that regenerates a new standing version V'(D2) in the window between the daily read (:194) and acquire (:208) leaves the daily binding the Tier-4 hold to the superseded date D, so the now-current V'(D2) reads no pointer at D2 and STANDS unheld = a safety fail-open. FIX (matching the cadence_runner precedent, which reads+regens+promotes inside the lock): move _read_standing + the snapshot capture INSIDE the cadence_lock critical section so read-compute-hold is one atomic section; re-run the 9 daily_monitor tests + the 7-mutation battery green. ESCALATION: if co-arming (glzi) ships without this fix, this is MEDIUM/HIGH (live safety fail-open on the Tier-4 hold). MUST land BEFORE glzi co-arms daily+weekly.

title: Harden POST /upload against cross-site denial-of-wallet (ADR-0030 F4)
description: PR #266 Tier-3 /review-pr finding F4 (Security SEC-266-01, conf 62 / impact 3; triaged DECISION — operator-owned). POST /upload accepts multipart/form-data (a CORS simple request, no preflight), and ADR-0030 wired a live ModelClient into the production entry, so an unrecognized-format cross-site upload now reaches client.extract_readings = a LIVE metered no-train call. A malicious page the operator visits while the loopback server runs can loop such uploads to drive operator-funded extraction (denial-of-wallet) and send attacker-chosen content to the no-train API. NOT a crown-jewel PII leak: the content is the attacker's own, the response is opaque cross-origin, nothing LANDS (the /confirm-extraction land path is application/json-CSRF-gated), and the bind is loopback-only. The recognized-format /upload arm was already cross-site-reachable pre-PR (ADR-0013-T4); this PR adds only the extract-spend consequence. FIX (operator decision — it is defense-in-depth on a loopback surface, needs sign-off per the no-unapproved-defensive-programming rule): add a Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin same-origin assertion to POST /upload (the one POST that can't use the application/json gate) — reject when Sec-Fetch-Site is present and not in {same-origin,none} OR Origin is present and not the loopback origin. Closes both the new extract-spend vector and the pre-existing recognized-format landing CSRF on the same route. Was NOT a merge-blocker (crown-jewel holds; bounded).

title: Build conversation summarization for the care agent context
description:
The care agent is currently fed the ENTIRE conversation thread verbatim every turn (e.g. 52 saved turns => 54 messages/turn). Prompt caching softens the cost but the payload still grows unbounded and will eventually exceed the model context window, silently dropping the oldest turns.

Build a summarization/retrieval layer over the conversation vault (vault/conversations/<thread>.md, scripts/serve/conversation_store.py) so the agent gets a compact, high-signal context instead of the full transcript:
- Roll older turns into a maintained summary (durable facts, decisions, directives), keep the most recent N turns verbatim.
- And/or retrieve only the turns relevant to the current turn from the vault, rather than feeding all of them.
- Wire into care_chat._care_messages (currently appends every conversation turn with no bound).

Motivation: cut wasted tokens per turn AND make the agent scale past the context window without forgetting the beginning. Related: the conversation vault (conversation_store) + the S104/S105 care-chat work.

description: PR#75 (S43 8j6) added router.summarize's value-level PII gate via pii_scan.scan_text, which reuses pii_scan's detection set: the @gmail.com contact pattern + operator-identity tokens. SEC-1 (Security, conf 88/impact 5): that set is NARROWER than the raw-PII classes router.EXCLUDED_RAW_PII names — a non-gmail email (x@protonmail.com), phone (+1 415 555 0199), or postal address typed into a free-text pass-through field (goal-targets/hard-limits) scores 0 and reaches BOTH the model (dispatch) and render (assemble). Reason it is a SEPARATE scope (not part of 8j6): the pii_scan token set predates this PR and is SHARED with the commit-hook scanner (scan); widening requires a coherent design decision about WHERE (scan vs scan_text vs both — the gmail-only choice for scan is deliberate to keep false-positives low on the shareable trunk) and WHAT patterns (false-positive risk on free-text values), i.e. a scanner-vocabulary redesign with its own review, not 8j6's 'integrate pii_scan' scope. NET: PR#75's gate is a strict improvement (catches the operator's own gmail+name, the realistic single-operator leak) and 8j6's 'unenforced assumption' defect IS closed; this bead completes the detection coverage. GATES LM-04 (real operator data) — resolve before first real data flows, same urgency as 8j6. Fix sketch: add generic-email + phone (E.164/NANP) patterns for the VALUE boundary (scan_text), decide commit-hook (scan) impact separately, weigh false-positives on goal-targets/hard-limits, keep single-source-of-truth, case-insensitive; consider NFKC for homograph. Add failing-capable tests per class.

title: DNS-rebinding bypasses content-type CSRF gate on secret-write routes (family)
description: Tier-3 Security (sec-pr48 SEC-01, PR #359 ADR-0048-T3): the secret-write routes _save_key + _save_tracker_token gate CSRF SOLELY on Content-Type==application/json. That stops classic cross-site CSRF (a cross-origin application/json POST forces a preflight the loopback server never answers — no do_OPTIONS, no CORS headers, verified) but NOT DNS rebinding: if the victim visits evil.com while the loopback server runs and the attacker rebinds evil.com->127.0.0.1, the fetch is SAME-ORIGIN, no preflight fires, and an application/json POST reaches the handler with no Origin/Host check -> attacker WRITES an attacker-chosen OAuth token into the operator's a-plus-maxing-<source>-oauth item (poisons the next tracker pull with attacker creds, or a garbage token = fail-closed sync DoS). BOUNDED: data-integrity / tracker-sync DoS, NOT token-exfil (status route is boolean-only + not CORS-readable, so the operator's token cannot be read back); requires the full rebind chain. PRE-EXISTING to the whole secret-write family (byte-identical posture in _save_key), NOT introduced by ADR-0048-T3 — T3 extends the class to N tokens. FIX (family-level, server-wide — NOT a T3-inline patch): extend the EXISTING _is_cross_site_origin(Origin) refusal (server.py:49, already wired to POST /upload at :238) to _save_key + _save_tracker_token, and/or add a Host-header 127.0.0.1/localhost allowlist (the standard DNS-rebinding defense; a same-origin rebind POST still carries Origin: evil.com and Host: evil.com). OPERATOR-SIGN-OFF-GATED: adding a control is defensive-programming-adjacent per the project rule; get sign-off before patching. Best landed with the o9b5 negative-CL fix + the 9yaw shared-body-helper as a single secret-write-family hardening PR. Note in the ADR-0013 threat model whether loopback-only is the accepted posture.

S53 (2026-06-12) — DESIGN ADOPTED (Walter: "adopt all four as recommended"; architect-profile analysis; full record: vault/decisions/2026-06-12-juc-trend-polarity-design.md). BUILD BRIEF: (1) new named registry-driven derivation for recent-trend-direction — sources = biomarker_meta.METADATA entries with non-None good_direction, read as biomarker::<name> via the caller-bound store_read (e3b convention); per-stream trend via the stream's own last two numeric readings + biomarker_meta.trend; worst-wins reduction (regressing > improving > flat); output pinned to TREND_DIRECTIONS. (4) Zero-stream case emits no-signal "flat" (the S39 wrong-affirmative raises — cross-item, unknown-polarity — stay). (5) Registry validity pin: every in-range entry carries a reference_range. SUMMARY_FIELD_SET and the closed vocabulary UNCHANGED (no MEDIUM-2 event). Revisit triggers in the decision note.

description: PR #266 Tier-3 /review-pr finding F5 (Code-Quality QUAL-2, conf 62 / impact 3; triaged DEFERRED). scripts/model/client.py _ClaudeNoTrainBackend now has THREE near-identical copies of the bounded-retry loop + the trailing 'raise ModelCallError(...) from None' + the verbatim ~6-line SEC-01 comment block: converse, deidentify, and the new extract_readings. The duplicated block carries the load-bearing SEC-01 invariant (constant message + from None to prevent a raw file/conversation/key leak in the traceback on a PUBLIC repo), which must now be kept in sync across 3 copies — a future edit to one (e.g. interpolating the exception for debuggability) that misses the others silently re-introduces a leak. title: Value-boundary postal-address detection (g5x residual)
description: PR#78 (g5x) DROPPED postal from pii_scan.scan_text (the router.summarize value boundary). Build a PRECISE postal detector with its own review: case-insensitive, anchored on a strong co-signal (US ZIP 5(-4) and/or 2-letter state token) so 'Dr Patel followup' does not match but '123 main st, springfield il 62704' (any case) does. Add per-form detection + negative-control (gym/honorific) tests. Gates the same LM-04 boundary as g5x.

title: handoff-audit should detect an accreted prior-session scope-contract body under the current header
description: S82 close-PR review gap: the S82 HANDOFF rotation left the prior S81 scope-contract BODY (a second 'Acceptance criteria:' block + Files/Invariants for /generate-plan) inline under the new '## Scope Contract — Session 82' header — a rotation clause-1 'replace, don't accrue' violation (the Edit replaced only the header+Goal line, not the full prior body). title: Governance test git-commits on the shared repo mid-suite (test_zero_edit_gate_reds_on_committed_routine_edit)
description: Surfaced S108 (during the 55qg full-suite run). tests/ingest/test_adapters.py::test_zero_edit_gate_reds_on_committed_routine_edit (line 568) writes to scripts/ingest/ingest.py, then runs REAL 'git add' + 'git commit' + 'git reset --mixed HEAD^' + 'git checkout' on the SHARED main checkout to prove the 0-edit numstat gate reds on a committed routine edit. Two hazards: (1) it flakes under the full-suite run when the index has PRE-STAGED changes — 'git commit' (no -a) commits whatever is staged, so it SWEEPS an in-flight staged file (this run swept a staged tests/serve/test_server.py into its probe commit, then un-staged it on reset) and the numstat baseline assertion transiently failed; passes clean standalone. (2) more seriously, a test that git-commits on the shared repo can perturb a developer's/agent's in-flight git state (staged set, HEAD) mid-run. Same flaky-under-contention family as the close-audit constituent flake (S107 bead) but here it's a pytest test mutating real git history. Fix candidates: isolate the probe to a throwaway temp git clone/worktree (not the shared checkout), or explicitly stash/restore + assert a clean index precondition, or 'git commit -o -- <path>' to commit ONLY the probe path (not the whole staged set). Low priority (passes standalone; the gate itself is correct), but a real repo-safety wrinkle.

title: CSRF: /upload forced-spend gap — multipart is CORS-simple, content-type gate can't cover it
description: Surfaced by the 55qg security review (S108). The CSRF content-type 415 gate (now on /chat, /care-chat, /generate-plan, /plan-loop, /save-key, /confirm-*) CANNOT protect POST /upload: /upload requires multipart/form-data, which is itself a CORS-SIMPLE content-type (no preflight). In production main() wires a live ModelClient (scripts/serve/__main__.py:77), so an upload with an UNRECOGNIZED file extension routes to client.extract_readings / extract_chunked.extract_all (route.py:216-223, dispatched server.py:232-234) — a metered no-train call. A cross-site fetch(url,{method:'POST',mode:'no-cors',body:<FormData with a fake unrecognized-ext file>}) sends multipart with NO preflight + NO gate → forces extraction spend on the operator's key (the opaque response doesn't matter — the server already spent). Same forced-spend threat class as 55qg. FIX (different mechanism, since /upload can't require application/json): an Origin/Referer allowlist check (loopback origins only) OR a required non-safelisted custom header, applied in do_POST BEFORE route.route_upload reaches the client. Completes the CSRF hardening of the spend surface.
close_reason: Landed via PR #294 (merge 1644ced): Origin CSRF gate on /upload — refuse 403 when Origin is present+non-loopback, before route_upload reaches the metered extract_readings. 3-lens review (security/correctness/test-coverage) all clean; exact-match property mutation-locked against substring+suffix refactors. Completes the CSRF hardening of the spend surface (with 55qg).

title: Negative Content-Length blocks the request thread at 8 server.py sites
description: Tier-2 QA (ADR-0048-T3 wave review, F1 — probe-observed): a 'Content-Length: -1' header passes int() and the '> _SETTINGS_MAX_BYTES' ceiling gate, then rfile.read(-1) BLOCKS the request thread until the client closes (no response written; store untouched). PRE-EXISTING idiom at 7 sites (server.py ~:251,:449,:500,:588,:638,:696,:956 _save_key) + the new 8th (_save_tracker_token ~:1041, which byte-mirrors _save_key per the ADR-0048-T3 recipe — to-spec, not a build defect). DoS-shaped sibling of the non-numeric-CL 400 case. FIX class-wide, not per-site: length < 0 -> 400 at all 8 sites or a centralized Content-Length parse helper, + a content_length='-1' test per surface (the ADR-0048-T3 suite has the non-numeric case to mirror). Own small PR; loopback-only exposure (ADR-0013) keeps severity low.
notes: Tier-2 SECURITY (sec-w48) corroborates + extends qa-w48 F1: (a) 'Content-Length: -1' skips the 413 ceiling (negative < _SETTINGS_MAX_BYTES) and rfile.read(-1) reads-to-EOF -> a 64KiB body (4x the 16KiB cap) is ingested AND WRITTEN (200 OK); (b) 'Content-Length: -5' -> uncaught ValueError at the read() -> dropped request thread with a stderr traceback, contradicting the 'thread is never dropped' docstring. Bounded/LOW: browser-UNREACHABLE (browsers compute Content-Length, forbid script override) -> only a local non-browser client (curl/script) that ALREADY owns the machine+keychain can send it; no privilege boundary crossed; no token leak on either path; ThreadingHTTPServer survives. SAME severity class as the DEFERRED bead zwow ('loopback-only single-operator self-DoS, deferred per no-defensive-programming-without-sign-off'). GATING CONSTRAINT: adding 'if length < 0 -> 400' is defensive validation against a browser-unreachable vector, so per the project no-defensive-programming rule it needs OPERATOR SIGN-OFF before the SE patches — do NOT silently add the guard. Best landed as a shared _read_settings_json_body helper across all 8 sites alongside the 9yaw confirm-body refactor, owned by the mirrored-template surface, not a T3-only patch.

title: [PR #297] confirm_plan_change: pointer flip precedes tailoring inside route except->400 (atomicity, dormant)
description: PR #297 /review-pr F6 (contracts, sub-threshold, DORMANT). scripts/serve/confirm.py::confirm_plan_change flips the plan-confirm:: pointer to 'confirmed' via set_decision, THEN fires _post_promote_tailoring — and the serve route _do_confirm_plan_change (server.py:695-707) wraps the whole call in try/except Exception -> 400. If a wired tailor_client raises during tailoring, the route returns 400 (client sees failure) while the pointer is ALREADY confirmed (plan stands); on retry the pending->confirmed transition short-circuits (decision_for == confirmed) and does NOT re-fire tailoring, so the confirmed domain is left permanently WITHOUT its tailored section. DORMANT: tailor_client=None everywhere in production (OQ-5 wiring deferred) so tailoring is a 0-spend pass-through that cannot raise; the loop is operator-gated (ADR-0039). Fail direction is SAFE (missing tailored egress, never an unconfirmed leak). NOTE: the flip-before-tailoring ORDER is DELIBERATE + REQUIRED — the tailoring emit-gate applies filter_confirmed, so a still-pending domain would be dropped; F6's 'fire tailoring before the flip' suggested fix is WRONG. Correct remediation belongs with the OQ-5 tailor_client-live-wiring (zsre family): make confirm+tailoring recoverable — return the confirmed decision (200) on a tailoring failure and/or re-fire tailoring on a retry of an already-confirmed-but-untailored domain — so a mid-tailoring crash is recoverable, not a permanently-untailored confirmed plan.

title: PF-S117-01: at a closed boundary under run-until-everything, RESUME the loop on the next item; surface operator-gated work descriptively, not as a stopping-decision

At the S116 close boundary — after 7 merged build cycles — I presented a checkpoint (high-value-done + operator-gated items teed up + 'if you'd rather I keep going, say so') that under the standing 'run the autonomous build loop until you have everything' directive read as a hand-back; the operator prodded 'so what are you asking me to do?'. I was NOT blocked (nothing required to continue; the operator-gated items are triggerable on the operator's timeline, not a block). REFINED LESSON: even a well-justified checkpoint that SURFACES operator-gated work (protocol-sanctioned) reads as a false-stop when it PAUSES the loop for an operator decision instead of continuing on the next item. GUARD: at a closed boundary under a run-until-everything directive with a non-empty queue, resume the loop on the next item (even a marginal one) immediately; note operator-gated work descriptively in the HANDOFF/close (teed up), NOT as a stopping-decision. Only stop for a GENUINE block (real spend / irreversible action / true ambiguity), and even then keep other autonomous work moving. 'Surface operator work' and 'keep running' are not mutually exclusive.

description: PR #268 Tier-3 bug-hunter finding (BUG-002), triaged DEFERRED. pdf_extract.py _run_pdftotext (~61) + _run_marker (~81) call subprocess.run(..., text=True) with no encoding, and md.read_text() (~86) likewise — decoded with the locale-preferred encoding under STRICT errors.
